strings.name: Peter Diamond
strings.summary: Diamond studies search frictions, public finance and social insurance, explaining why unemployment and vacancies coexist. He connects theory to pensions, retirement and social-security reform. He shared the 2010 economics Nobel with Mortensen and Pissarides and remained involved in tax-policy advocacy in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Studies labour-market search and social insurance, influencing unemployment analysis and pension design.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Yale mathematics BA (1960); MIT economics PhD (1963).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Search-market framework
strings.highlights.h1.text: Includes the time and cost of finding partners in employment and equilibrium analysis.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Pensions and social security
strings.highlights.h2.text: Examines retirement reform through insurance, incentives and distributional goals.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Signed wealth-tax letter
strings.timeline.t1.text: Joined fellow laureates backing a California billionaire-tax proposal, expressing a policy position.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Shared economics Nobel
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won with Dale Mortensen and Christopher Pissarides for markets with search frictions.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Pension-reform book
strings.timeline.t3.text: With Nicholas Barr, examined principles, policy choices and reform trade-offs.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Search-equilibrium paper
strings.timeline.t4.text: Studied aggregate-demand management in the Journal of Political Economy.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Congressional social-security advice
strings.timeline.t5.text: Began consulting Congress on social-security reform.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined MIT
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began long service, later becoming Institute Professor and retiring in 2011.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctorate and Berkeley appointment
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned MIT’s doctorate before becoming an assistant professor at Berkeley.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed Yale mathematics degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Built mathematical foundations for subsequent economic theory.
